main_text.p: Quì verò sic, ô homo? Si enim inq;[?] Misericordiam erga humanum genus exercuit, & bonitatem ac liberalitatem suam nobis commendare voluit: Deus: cur prorsus gratuito, quidem potuit (non autem potuit, ut jam stultum) scelera hominibus non condonavit? Sin vindictam & severitatem suam in injurias ulciscendis, & delictis puniendis, ad sui nominis gloriam offendere statuit, cur non eos ipsos ulcisci[?] & supplicio afficere aggressus est, qui deliquerunt, & ejus Majestatem laserant?

Audisti rationem; quia impunitiq; dimittuntur, credunt in filium Deum Sponsorem suum, qui pœnas ipsorum peccatis debitas, ultro in se sustulit, & luit, adeoq; pro ipsis satisfecit, & re-piscunt. Ex parte itaq; Dei, justitiæ jus respondet nostri sponsoris satisfa-ctio. Ex parte nostra, postulato Dei, respondet per gratiam ipsius in fœdere promissam, fides & obedientia ejus.

II. Non posse corporalem pœnam nisi ab eo ipso exigi, qui peccavit, pro-batur testimonio ipsius Dei, Ezech. 18. Ubi multis verbis declarat, semper esse {a}[?] quitates filiorum in patribus, nec patrum in filiis punire, si filii similes patrum scelestorum nō su-Obiectio de corporali pœna quod non possit exigi nisi a pecca-tore ipso. Probatur.

page.notes: Top of page stained and foxed; the first and last lines of the italic passage are partly faded. Doubtful readings: "inq;" after "Si enim" (last letters unclear); "ulcisci[?]" at the line break; "Ubi multis verbis declarat" line, where the words after "declarat," are not clearly legible and were partly guessed, so the reading "semper esse" is uncertain and marked; the reference mark before "quitates" is not clearly visible in the scan and is doubtful. The catchword at the lower right ("ruit") is only partly visible and is not transcribed. Right edge shows the neighbouring page's text and is omitted. Printed page number "318" is partly obscured.
